props.gloss_en: R' Yehoshua b. Chananya to the emperor: you will see the Persians press you into service, capture you, and make you herd unclean animals with a golden staff
[the emperor] thought about it all day, and at night he saw it
Shmuel to King Shapur: you will see the Romans come and take you captive and make you grind date-pits in a golden mill
[Shapur] thought about it all day, and at night he saw it
bar Hedya was an interpreter of dreams: for one who paid him he interpreted favourably, for one who did not, unfavourably
Abaye and Rava saw a dream; Abaye gave him a zuz and Rava did not

'your ox shall be slain before your eyes' (Deut 28:31) read in their dream: to Rava -- your business will be lost and you will not eat for grief; to Abaye -- your business will profit and you will not eat for joy
'you shall beget sons and daughters...' (Deut 28:41): to Rava -- literally [captivity]; to Abaye -- your children will be many and your daughters married to outsiders, as if gone into captivity

'your sons and daughters shall be given to another people' (Deut 28:32): to Abaye -- they will be married to your wife's kin, which is like another people; to Rava -- your wife will die and your children come into the hands of another woman
Rav: 'your sons and daughters shall be given to another people' -- this is the father's wife
'go, eat your bread with joy' (Eccl 9:7): to Abaye -- profit, and you will read the verse from joy; to Rava -- loss, and you will drink and read to allay your fear
'you shall carry much seed out into the field' (Deut 28:38): to Abaye from its beginning, to Rava from its end
'you shall have olive trees throughout your borders' (Deut 28:40): to Abaye from its beginning, to Rava from its end

'all the peoples of the earth shall see' (Deut 28:10): to Abaye -- you will be known as head of the academy; to Rava -- the king's treasury will be broken into, you will be seized as a thief, and everyone will reason a fortiori from you
the next day the king's treasury was broken into, and they came and seized Rava
lettuce on the mouth of barrels: to Abaye -- your business will double like lettuce; to Rava -- bitter like lettuce
meat on the mouth of barrels: to Abaye -- your wine will be sweet and all will buy meat and wine from you; to Rava -- your wine will sour and all will buy meat to eat with it
a barrel hanging on a palm: to Abaye -- your business will rise like a palm; to Rava -- sweet [cheap] like dates
a pomegranate sprouting on the mouth of barrels: to Abaye -- your business will be dear like a pomegranate; to Rava -- sour like a pomegranate
a barrel fallen into a pit: to Abaye -- your wares will be sought, as the saying goes 'bread fell into a pit and was not found'; to Rava -- your wares will spoil and you will throw them into a pit
a donkey-foal standing at their heads braying: to Abaye -- you will be king [head of the academy] with a spokesman standing over you
to Rava: [the passage] 'peter chamor' is erased from your tefillin
bar Hedya: the vav of 'peter chamor' is certainly erased from your tefillin

Rava alone, unpaid: outer door fell -- your wife will die; molars and teeth fell -- your children will die; two doves flying -- you will divorce two wives; two turnip-heads -- you will swallow two blows
that day Rava found two blind men quarrelling in the study hall, went to separate them, and they struck him two blows
Rava, as they raised their staffs again: enough -- I saw two

Rava, having paid: wall fell -- you will acquire property without bounds; Abaye's mansion fell -- Abaye will die and his academy come to you; my mansion fell and all took its bricks -- your teachings will spread through the world; my head split -- a feather will come out of the pillow; the Egyptian hallel read to me -- miracles will be done for you
bar Hedya, sailing with Rava: why am I with a man for whom miracles are done?
all dreams follow the mouth -- found written in the book that fell from bar Hedya
Rava: wicked man -- it depended on you, and you caused me so much suffering
Rava: I forgive you everything except Rav Chisda's daughter [my wife]; may it be [God's] will that this man be delivered into the hands of a kingdom that has no mercy on him
bar Hedya: we have it by tradition that a sage's curse comes about even when it is baseless
bar Hedya: I will rise and go into exile
the Master: exile atones for sin
in Rome the keeper of the king's wardrobe told him his dreams; twice bar Hedya asked a zuz, was refused, and said nothing; the third time he said: a worm has fallen upon all the silks
the wardrobe-keeper, being led to execution: why me? bring the one who knew and did not say
the king's men to bar Hedya: because of your zuz the king's silks were ruined
they tied two cedars together, bound his legs to them and released the rope; he split and fell in two
R' Yishmael to Ben Dama (my two cheeks fell off): two Roman legions plotted evil against you, and they died

Rebbi to bar Kappara: nose fell off -- anger has departed from you; hands cut off -- you will not need your handiwork; legs cut off -- you ride a horse; 'you die in Adar and will not see Nisan' -- you will die in glory (אדרותא) and not come to trial (נסיון)

R' Yishmael's readings of the min's nine dreams (oil to olives, plucking and swallowing a star, eyes kissing, kissing the moon, treading in myrtle shade, shade above tree below, ravens and doves round his bed, two doves flying): incest, kidnapping and selling an Israelite, adultery, a betrothed girl, and wives dismissed without a get
R' Yishmael to the min (I was peeling eggs): you strip the dead
a woman came and said: this cloak you are wearing belongs to so-and-so, who died and whom you stripped
R' Yishmael (your father left you property in Cappadocia; you have none there and he never went): kappa is a beam, deka is ten -- go look at the head of the tenth beam, it is full of coins
he went and found it full of coins

R' Chanan: a bird

the baraita (five things said of the ox): it gored him -- he will have sons who gore [one another] in Torah
the baraita (five things said of the ox): it bit him -- suffering is coming upon him
the baraita (five things said of the ox): it kicked him -- a distant journey awaits him
the baraita (five things said of the ox): he rode it -- he will rise to greatness
a baraita: [one who dreams] he rode it -- will die

'behold your king comes... triumphant and saved, lowly and riding on a donkey' (Zech 9:9)
one who sees in a dream a cat, where it is called shunra -- a fine song (שירה נאה) will be made for him
one who sees in a dream where it is called shinra -- a change for the worse (שינוי רע)

one who sees in a dream black grapes in season -- good
one who sees in a dream black grapes out of season -- bad

one who sees in a dream a red horse walking -- good
one who sees in a dream a red horse galloping -- hard

one who sees a camel in a dream -- death was decreed on him from Heaven and he was saved from it

Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: from here -- 'the Lord also (גם) has put away your sin; you shall not die' (II Sam 12:13)
one who sees Pinchas in a dream -- a wonder was done for him
one who sees an elephant (פיל) in a dream -- wonders (פלאות) were done for him

one who puts on tefillin in a dream should expect greatness

R' Eliezer the Great: this is the tefillin of the head
one who prays in a dream -- it is a good sign for him

'your iniquity is taken away (וסר עונך) and your sin atoned' (Isa 6:7)

a choice vine-branch -- he should expect the Messiah
'binding his foal to the vine, his donkey's colt to the choice vine' (Gen 49:11)

large ones -- his business will grow like a pomegranate
halves: if he is a Torah scholar, he should expect Torah

and if he is an ignoramus, he should expect mitzvot
'your temples (רקתך) are like a slice of pomegranate' (Song 4:3)
what is רקתך? even the empty ones (ריקנין) among you are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate
small olives -- his business will be fruitful, grow and last like olives
and this [applies to] the fruit
but [olive] trees -- he will have many children
'your children like olive saplings' (Ps 128:3)
some say: one who sees an olive tree in a dream -- a good name goes out for him
'a leafy olive tree, fair with goodly fruit, the Lord called your name' (Jer 11:16)
one who sees olive oil -- he should expect the light of Torah
'let them bring you pure olive oil [for the light]' (Ex 27:20)
one who sees dates (תמרים) -- his sins are ended (תמו)
'your iniquity is ended, daughter of Zion' (Lam 4:22)

goats -- years will be blessed for him
'and there will be goats' milk enough for your food' (Prov 27:27)
one who sees myrtle -- his property will prosper; and if he has none, an inheritance will fall to him from elsewhere
and that is where he saw them on their stems
one who sees an etrog -- he is splendid (הדור) before his Maker
'the fruit of a splendid (הדר) tree, branches of palms' (Lev 23:40)
one who sees a lulav -- he has but one heart for his Father in heaven
one who sees a goose in a dream should expect wisdom
'wisdom cries aloud in the street' (Prov 1:20)
and one who has relations with it will be head of the academy

one who enters a city -- his desires are fulfilled
'and He led them to their desired haven' (Ps 107:30)
one who shaves his head -- a good sign for him
his head and beard -- for him and all his family
one who sits in a small boat -- a good name goes out for him
in a large boat -- for him and all his family
and this only where it rides high
one who relieves himself in a dream -- a good sign for him
'he that is bent down shall speedily be loosed' (Isa 51:14)
and this only where he did not wipe
one who goes up to a roof in a dream rises to greatness
[if] he came down -- he comes down from his greatness
Abaye and Rava both: once he went up, he went up
one who tears his garments -- his sentence is torn up
one who stands naked in a dream: in Babylonia -- he stands without sin
in the Land of Israel -- naked without mitzvot
one seized by a soldier -- protection is made for him
put in a neck-iron -- they added protection to his protection
and this only a neck-iron, but a mere rope, no

a forest -- becomes head of the kalla students

it was Rav Sheshet who saw a snake in his dream and killed it

there is one who drinks it and it is good for him

schemas.gloss_en: גמירי דקללת חכם אפילו בחנם היא באה, וכל שכן רבא דבדינא קא לייט -- a sage's curse comes about even when baseless; all the more so Rava's, who cursed justly

supports.gloss_en: דאמר רבא אמר רבי ירמיה בר אבא אמר רב: בניך ובנותיך נתונים לעם אחר -- זו אשת האב; bar Hedya's reading to Rava rests on Rav's reading of the verse
איקום ואגלי, דאמר מר: גלות מכפרת עון
ותניא, רבי אליעזר הגדול אומר: אלו תפילין שבראש -- the baraita that ties 'the Lord's name is called upon you' to tefillin
מאי רקתך -- אפילו ריקנין שבך מלאים מצות כרמון: the derasha that makes the verse speak of mitzvot

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דרכיב הוא לתורא, הא דרכיב תורא לדידיה -- he rides the ox (greatness) vs. the ox rides him (death)

objections.gloss_en: והתניא: כל מיני חיות יפין לחלום חוץ מן הפיל ומן הקוף!

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דמסרג, הא דלא מסרג -- saddled vs. not saddled
מאי סדורין -- סדורין לימחל: arrayed [in order] to be forgiven

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רב ששת: כל שכן שנכפלה פרנסתו -- if a bite doubles it, killing it all the more so

answered_by.gloss_en: ולא היא, רב ששת הוא דחזא חויא בחלמיה וקטליה -- it is not so: Rav Sheshet had himself dreamt he killed a snake

objections.gloss_en: והאמר מר: הרואה פיל בחלום פלא נעשה לו!

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דמסרג, הא דלא מסרג

objections.gloss_en: והאמר רב: לא איעתרי עד דחזאי ראשי לפתות!

answered_by.gloss_en: כי חזא -- בכנייהו חזא: when he saw them, he saw them on their stems
